question: How did the loop do yesterday?
short: One day of loop deliveries: what the loop delivered on its own, which runs were wasted, where a person stepped in, and the few changes that would have saved runs.
lede: The loop should move work forward alone and ask a person only for a real decision. This report measures how close one day came, names the causes, and keeps both over time, so a fix that holds and a cause that returns are both visible.
asks: How did the loop do yesterday?
Why did the preparer keep retrying last Tuesday?
steps: Collects one calendar day from GitHub in your local time, yesterday by default: runs, outcomes, comments and merged PRs. A day reads the same whenever it is collected.
Names a cause for every delivery that needed a person, every wasted run and every reviewer send-back, from run summaries, denied commands and retrospectives.
Proposes at most four changes, each giving clearer authority, better wording, fewer instructions or more autonomy. It never adds a role, label, gate or checklist.
Renders the report, opens it in your browser and leaves a JSON record of the day next to it.
With the Uberblick MCP server, stores the day in a Delivery report document, so KPIs and recurring causes show up over time.
facts: items the loop delivered with no person stepping in
runs that moved nothing forward, and what they cost
each time the loop asked a person, and how long it waited
first run to delivery, without that wait
agent minutes summed over the day
runs that hit a permission denial
needs: python3 and an authenticated gh. Reads GitHub only.
the Uberblick MCP server, to keep each day in a document and chart KPIs over time.
report.html in your browser and report.json, a record of the day.
